subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Chris Tan <chris.tan@fintechco.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 14:05:00 -0700
Subject: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks again for your time today, Chris and Asha — great demo discussion. Per our call, I wanted to capture the performance / SLO items we covered and propose concrete next steps (mutual action plan). Attached is a draft SLO checklist (fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx) and a recording of the demo.

Quick recap of the performance targets you mentioned and our ask for confirmation: 
- Latency: target P95 end-to-end response latency <= 250ms for 1–2k token requests (batching disabled for low-latency flows).
- Throughput: baseline 200 QPS sustained for non-batched requests; peak burst to 500 QPS.
- Concurrency: 8 concurrent streaming sessions for the primary user path.
- Streaming: need partial token streaming (server->client) with first-token latency <= 80ms for streaming RPCs.
- SLA/availability: 99.9% for production endpoints.

Proposed MAP items (owners + ETA):
1) Confirm final SLO numbers and sample payloads — Owner: Chris (FintechCo) — ETA: 2027-10-08
2) Provide sample traffic trace (1 hour) + representative prompt set — Owner: Asha — ETA: 2027-10-08
3) Redwood to run a perf run against chosen model variant and produce a 1-page perf summary — Owner: Dylan Brooks (Redwood) — ETA: 2027-10-11
4) Evaluation environment (trial Dedicated / sandbox) set up and credentials — Owner: Logan Wright (Redwood) — ETA: 2027-10-12
5) Procurement / commercial check-in — Owner: Chris / FintechCo procurement — ETA: 2027-10-20

Can you confirm the latency/throughput/concurrency numbers above are correct? If anything needs to change, we’ll adjust the checklist before Dylan runs the perf tests. If those look right, I’ll schedule the MAP kickoff for next Wednesday (2027-10-12) and loop in infra/procurement.

Thanks —
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com | (415) 555-0113

Attachments: fintechco-slo-checklist.xlsx, demo-recording.mp4

From: Chris Tan <chris.tan@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechco.com>
Date: Tue, 05 Oct 2027 15:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Marissa — thanks for the clear recap and the checklist. Quick confirmations and a couple of clarifying questions: 
1) The P95 <= 250ms target is specifically for end-to-end REST requests that return full payloads, correct? For streaming use-cases we care more about first-byte/first-token latency (we'd like first-token <= 80ms) and sustained tail behavior.
2) For throughput, the 200 QPS baseline assumes short prompts (~200 tokens). For longer prompts (1–2k tokens) sustained QPS will be lower — we can provide representative traffic.
3) Concurrency 8 is per-customer; we may need to scale to 20 during peak for a short pilot.

Next steps — we’ll provide the sample traces and prompt set by Friday (2027-10-08). We also need to understand whether the eval environment will be Hosted (Redwood API) or a short-term Dedicated pool for more realistic GPU-bound perf testing. If Dedicated is required, budget / procurement will take longer.

Asha, I loop you here — do you want to prioritize a Dedicated eval or is Hosted sufficient for the perf run?

Thanks,
Chris
Director of Engineering | FintechCo
chris.tan@fintechco.com

On Tue, Oct 5, 2027 at 2:05 PM Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com> wrote:
> Thanks again for your time today, Chris and Asha — great demo discussion...

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwood.com>
To: Chris Tan <chris.tan@fintechco.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechco.com>
Cc: logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 08:27:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Hi Chris / Asha — Dylan from Redwood infra here. Quick answers to help you decide on Hosted vs Dedicated for the perf run and to confirm how we’ll measure the SLOs: 

- Latency: When we say P95 <= 250ms we mean end-to-end service response measured at the Redwood edge for the REST path (including model decode time). For streaming we measure first-token latency separately; we can validate first-token <= 80ms with streaming enabled.
- Throughput: Our hosted API can hit the baseline 200 QPS for short prompts on standard model variants; for the long prompt profile (1–2k tokens) we expect lower sustained QPS. For realistic GPU-bound performance we recommend a short Dedicated pool for the perf run — it provides deterministic concurrency and removes noisy neighbor variability.
- Concurrency & scaling: We can configure autoscale to maintain 8 concurrent streaming sessions with a burst to 20 for pilot windows. For the perf run we’ll set concurrency targets and simulate gradual ramp to observe tail behavior.
- Batching: We will disable server-side batching for the low-latency streaming path during the test; for cost-efficiency in production we can enable batching for non-interactive flows.
- Fallbacks: If p95 or first-token numbers do not meet targets on a single model, we’ll test a quantized variant and a smaller-parameter low-latency model for degraded-quality fast-path.

I’ll take point on the perf summary (see MAP item 3). Can you share the sample trace + prompt set and a target test window (2–4 hours) so I can schedule dedicated capacity? Also indicate whether you prefer Hosted trial or Dedicated eval — if Dedicated, we’ll start procurement conversations in parallel.

Thanks —
Dylan Brooks
Senior SRE, Inference Performance | Redwood Inference
dylan.brooks@redwood.com

Attachment: proposed-test-plan.md (referenced in SLO checklist)

From: Asha Patel <asha.patel@fintechco.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Chris Tan <chris.tan@fintechco.com>
Cc: dylan.brooks@redwood.com, logan.wright@redwood.com
Date: Wed, 06 Oct 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: FintechCo — Post-demo performance recap & SLO checklist

Thanks everyone — confirmation from our side:
- Confirming SLO targets: P95 end-to-end <= 250ms (REST short prompts), first-token streaming <= 80ms, baseline throughput 200 QPS for short prompts, concurrency 8 with burst to 20 during pilot.
- We will provide the 1-hour sample trace and canonical prompt set by EOD Friday (2027-10-08).
- We prefer a short Dedicated eval for the perf run to mirror our production GPU environment; procurement is aware and will start the rapid approval (targeting 2027-10-20).

Please schedule the MAP kickoff on 2027-10-12 and send invites for a 30-minute SLO signoff + perf plan sync. Once Dylan shares the perf summary we’ll confirm decision criteria for GA (latency, cost per 1k tokens, reliability).

Appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Asha Patel
Head of Product | FintechCo
asha.patel@fintechco.com
